thread:
customer-john: Hey team, since yesterday we're seeing a big jump in p95 on streaming endpoints. TTFB looks fine for the first chunk but subsequent chunks arrive in big bursts — non-streaming responses are actually faster end-to-end. This started after a model rollout. Anyone seen this?
elaine-support: sorry to hear that, @customer-john. Can you share an example request id and a short curl or SDK call you used? Also which model and region?
customer-john: req=rc-2026-05-03-1234, model=redwood-extended-1, region=us-west-2. SDK call is the default streaming chat example. I'll paste a minimal curl in a sec.
elaine-support: thanks — tagging infra: @samir-eng @ingrid-sre for perf traces.
samir-eng: looking. Can you confirm if this is observed from multiple clients or only their app? Also need trace IDs from console (trace-id header) if available.
customer-john: curl example:
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-extended-1","input":"long prompt here","stream":true}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat
```
customer-john: trace-id: trace-7791, full logs attached to support ticket.
ingrid-sre: initial observation from our side: p50 unchanged, p95 jump ~450ms. The pattern looks like first byte fast (~50ms) then a jittery tail with 2-3 big gaps. Reproduced with our internal synthetic client hitting same model.
maria-ml: note that the recent rollout included a KV-cache optimization and small-change batching thresholds. Could be related to chunking behavior and flush signals.
samir-eng: I ran a local repro against the same model. With HTTP/1.1 streaming we see regular small chunks. With HTTP/2 and multiplexing, chunks are coalesced and then flushed infrequently — looks like a TLS framing/recording effect combined with our write buffer heuristic.
elaine-support: @samir-eng do you have the exact command or script you used to reproduce? Customer needs a mitigation ASAP.
samir-eng: repro script (abridged):
```
#!/bin/bash
for i in {1..5}; do
  curl -s -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-extended-1","input":"generate lots","stream":true}' \
    https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat | tee out$i
  sleep 0.5
done
```
Comparing out files shows first chunk then pauses ~200-400ms before next flush. When forcing `--http1.1` in curl gaps disappear.
ingrid-sre: that suggests HTTP/2 semantics + our proxy interaction. We had a recent change to the proxy keepalive and output flush thresholds (PR #4248). I'll roll that log and compare.
alex-pm: can we avoid rolling back but offer the customer a config toggle to force sync/disable-h2 for a quick mitigation?
samir-eng: yes — we can add a response header / SDK param for customers to opt out of multiplexed streaming routes: X-Redwood-Stream-Mode: sync or add a query param `streaming_protocol=http1`. I'll validate with infra if safe.
elaine-support: I've passed the workaround to the customer: set streaming=false to get non-streaming responses or use `streaming_protocol=http1` for chunked streaming under HTTP/1.1 while we investigate.
customer-john: thanks — non-streaming works and p95 returns to previous values. But we need streaming to work for low-latency user updates. Any ETA?
maria-ml: hypothesis: our runtime batches/flushes partially based on whether the connection is detected as h2 multiplexed. Combined with kernel TLS record coalescing and proxy heuristics, small tokens can be buffered and delayed. The KV-cache change changed chunk boundaries, exposing the proxy-buffering regression.
samir-eng: digging deeper — traces show our runtime is calling flush() after every token, but nginx/edge proxy only sends frames when either N bytes accumulate or after 150ms. HTTP/1.1 TCP_NODELAY bypasses that because it uses small TLS records more aggressively.
ingrid-sre: lined up a quick patch to the edge proxy to lower the flush threshold to 30ms for streaming lanes. Deploying to canary now.
sre-bot: deploy canary started: deploy-2026-05-04-edge-flush-30ms -> 1/3 hosts
sre-bot: deploy canary success: 1/3 hosts healthy
ingrid-sre: canary metrics: p95 for streaming reduced from +450ms to +90ms on the canary host. Rolling to remaining hosts.
sre-bot: deploy progress: 3/3 hosts -> success
samir-eng: after rollout, reran repro script against customer region. Observed steady small chunks, gaps gone. Verified both HTTP/2 and HTTP/1.1 showing similar behavior.
elaine-support: shared update with customer and asked them to test.
customer-john: confirmed — streaming latency fixed for our workload. p95 back to normal. Huge thanks. :tada:
alex-pm: follow-ups: 1) add e2e test that runs streaming over h2 + synthetic small-token sequences, 2) add a flag in console to force http1 streaming per-deployment, 3) postmortem of the KV-cache/batching interaction.
maria-ml: agree on tests — I'll add a nightly job that exercises small-chunk patterns.
ingrid-sre: postmortem draft will include timeline of rollout, PR #4248 interaction, detection via customer report, canary rollback risk (none), and mitigation.
elaine-support: closing the support ticket once customer confirms in 24h. Will reopen if anything flares.
customer-john: closing from our side too. Great response time.
alex-pm: nice coordination. Logging all artifacts into the incident tracker and will schedule a retro with infra + runtime + ml next week.
